scenario: Floa utility view layout at narrow floating browser content size
runtime: Google Chrome headless, local utility HTML and CSS

viewport.reason: 420x500 outer window with 117px shared toolbar and tab strip

pages.name: Notes
pages.result: rendered; note list and editor remain within captured content viewport; formatting toolbar scrolls horizontally

pages.name: Reader
pages.result: rendered; compact sidebar; controls remain horizontally scrollable; empty library description constrained to content column

pages.name: Window Mirror
pages.result: rendered; empty source state remains visible; no capture permission requested

limitations: This checks utility document layout in Chromium, not Electron WebContentsView switching or persistence.
The shared Floa toolbar and tab strip are excluded from the screenshots; their 117px height is accounted for in the viewport.
Electron application window was not shown or focused.

Real OS keyboard delivery was not tested because doing so would require focusing the application. Shortcut matching and handling were exercised through the same installed before-input-event listener using the isolated headless-only test hook.
Screen Recording permissions and live Window Mirror capture were not granted or exercised.

integratedShell.runtime: actual index.html, workspace.js, renderer.js with mocked browserApp IPC in Chrome headless
integratedShell.result: browser and utility tab groups render in one strip; browser action row clips off-screen but is horizontally scrollable
limitations: Renderer IPC is mocked; this does not exercise Electron BrowserWindow or WebContentsView attachment.
Home content in the shell capture sits behind the native content view in the real app.

Window Mirror showed its Screen Recording permission state in the isolated test profile; no permission was granted.
